description: Merchandise Marks Act (1862) Amendment Bill (Bill 142) ordered and read a first time in the Commons, brought in by Baron Henry De Worms (Board of Trade) and the Attorney General
source: HC Deb 31 Jan 1887 vol 310 c383
note: Verified at source. A Select Committee on this bill (17 members, Mundella among them) was appointed on 5 Apr 1887 (https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/commons/1887/apr/05/merchandise-marks-act-1862-amendment-bill). Other bills: Mundella's private bill, ordered 22 Feb 1887 (https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/commons/1887/feb/22/merchandise-fraudulent-marks-bill), and the Attorney General's Merchandise Marks Law Consolidation and Amendment Bill (Bill 194), read a first time on 11 Mar 1887 (https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/commons/1887/mar/11/merchandise-marks-law-consolidation-and). The Consolidation bill went to the Lords on 12 Jul 1887 and appears to be the bill enacted. I did not check how the Select Committee's text passed into it. If the Act's own bill is wanted, use 1887-03-11.

description: Patents and Designs Bill (Bill 121): Lloyd George (Board of Trade) moved for leave under the ten-minute rule; presented and read a first time the same day
source: HC Deb 19 Mar 1907 vol 171 cc683-7
note: Verified at source. Second reading 17 Apr 1907. A separate Patents and Designs (No. 2) Bill dates from 11 Apr 1907, and a consolidation bill followed in August. I found no earlier formal committee step in 1907.

description: Chamberlain, as Chancellor, announced the general 10% ad valorem import duty in the Commons and moved the Ways and Means (money) resolution
source: HC Deb 4 Feb 1932 vol 261 cc279-96
note: Verified at source. The bill itself (Bill 23) was presented and read a first time on 10 Feb 1932 (https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/commons/1932/feb/10/import-duties-bill). Use 1932-02-10 if bill introduction is the strict criterion. The earlier Cabinet committee work of Jan 1932 is informal and was not checked.

description: Brussels sugar-bounty conference reconvened as a new session of the 1898 conference, all Powers except Russia attending; it produced the convention signed 5 Mar 1902
source: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1911, 'Sugar' (vol. 26 p. 61, Wikisource copy), seen only as a search excerpt
note: Secondary source: the EB1911 page could not be fetched here. A Commons question of 1902 refers to the British delegate's statement on 17 Dec 1901. Verified at source: the Belgian proposal to reassemble the Brussels Conference was reported in the Commons on 21 Feb 1901 (URL given). Earlier conference: opened at Brussels on 7 Jun 1898 (EB1911, secondary) and ended without agreement. Signing date 5 Mar 1902 verified in https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/commons/1902/nov/24/brussels-sugar-convention.

description: Japan formally applied for an invitation to negotiate accession to GATT
source: FRUS 1955-57, accession negotiations opened 21 Feb 1955 (see note)
note: Incumbent-side start used: accession negotiations opened 21 Feb 1955 (FRUS). Japan's own application of July 1952 is the challenger's step. Verified at source to the month (the source gives no day). Later steps: the application was taken up at the 7th Session in Oct 1952, and provisional accession came in 1953 (not checked). The accession tariff negotiations opened at Geneva on 21 Feb 1955 (FRUS 1955-57 vol IX doc 33, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1955-57v09/d33, which also notes the UK decision of Nov 1954 not to negotiate). The protocol was signed 7 Jun 1955 and took effect 10 Sep 1955. Use 1955-02-21 if the accession negotiations are the preferred start.

description: Japanese voluntary controls on cotton textile exports to the US for 1956, adopted under US pressure
source: FRUS 1955-57 vol IX doc 60 (Dulles to Gov. Timmerman, 17 Apr 1956)
note: Not verified. FRUS says Japan 'voluntarily restricted the export of cotton goods to the United States in January 1956'. FRUS vol IX doc 68 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1955-57v09/d68) says Japan formally informed the US of its 1956 restrictions on 16 May 1956. A secondary article (Business History Conference, 'Growth of VERs ... 1956-1969', thebhc.org, could not be fetched) reportedly dates the Japanese announcement to Dec 1955. I found no primary date for when US pressure or talks began.

description: US-Japan official discussions leading to Japan's five-year cotton textile export control programme, announced 16 Jan 1957
source: FRUS 1955-57 vol IX doc 99 (Blackman, Commerce, 12 Jul 1957)
note: Year-level only. FRUS says the programme 'was developed after months of discussions' and refers to the Japanese 'original proposal during the 1956 discussions'. The talks were held mainly in Washington through the Japanese Embassy (FRUS vol XXIII doc 109, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1955-57v23p1/d109). The opening month was not verified. A related formal track: the Tariff Commission's velveteen escape-clause recommendation of 24 Oct 1956.

description: Treasury received the antidumping complaint (Electronic Industries Association) on monochrome and colour TV receivers from Japan
source: Treasury LTFV determination, 35 FR 18549 (5 Dec 1970)
note: Verified at source ('Information was received on March 22, 1968'). Tariff Commission injury finding 4 Mar 1971 (36 FR 4576); dumping finding T.D. 71-76, 36 FR 4597 (10 Mar 1971), https://www.govinfo.gov/link/fr/36/4597.

description: Section 201 escape-clause petition on TV receivers (USITC inv. TA-201-19) by COMPACT, a union and company coalition (unions led by the Industrial Union Dept, AFL-CIO)
source: USITC Pub. 808 (1977)
note: Not verified: usitc.gov and the law-journal hosts were blocked in this session. Found: inv. TA-201-19; the report's data run to Jan-Sep 1976, which fits a filing in late 1976; ITC report to the President dated 22 Mar 1977 (Carter memo, presidency.ucsb.edu, search excerpt); OMA signed 20 May 1977, effective 1 Jul 1977 (Proclamation 4511). Check the petition and institution dates in the introduction of Pub. 808.

description: State Department talks with Japanese and European steel producer associations, leading to letters capping exports to the US for 1969-71
source: Consumers Union v. Kissinger, 506 F.2d 136 (D.C. Cir. 1974)
note: Secondary: the court opinion was seen only as a search excerpt, since justia was blocked here. Excerpt: 'State Department officials entered into discussions that lasted from June to December, 1968'. Talks were led by Deputy Under Secretary Nathaniel Samuels. The 14 Jan 1969 announcement and transmission to Congress was not checked against a primary text.

description: Treasury Secretary Blumenthal proposed, and Carter approved (undated initials), an interagency steel task force under Treasury Under Secretary Anthony Solomon, with proposals due by late November
source: FRUS 1977-80 vol III doc 63 (Blumenthal to Carter, 29 Sep 1977)
note: Verified at source for the memo date. Carter's approval is undated, so the date marks the proposal, not a dated approval. A White House steel conference was held 13 Oct 1977 (secondary). The Solomon report, released 6 Dec 1977, recommended trigger prices (FRUS doc 79, 1 Dec 1977, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1977-80v03/d79). Treasury announced the first trigger prices 3 Jan 1978 (secondary).

description: UAW filed a Section 201 petition on passenger cars and light trucks; ITC instituted inv. TA-201-44 on 30 Jun 1980
source: USITC, Report to the President TA-201-44, 45 FR 85194 (24 Dec 1980)
note: Verified at source. Ford's petition was received 4 Aug 1980; Ford was treated as a co-petitioner (notice 45 FR 55873, 21 Aug 1980). Institution notice 45 FR 45731 (7 Jul 1980). ITC negative determination dated 3 Dec 1980.

description: SIA filed a Section 301 petition alleging restricted access to Japan's semiconductor market
source: GATT Panel Report L/6309, Japan - Trade in Semi-conductors (24 Mar 1988), para. 11
note: Verified at source (OCR of the scanned GATT report). Same paragraph: Micron's 64K DRAM antidumping petition 24 Jun 1985; EPROM antidumping petition by Intel, AMD and National Semiconductor 30 Sep 1985; Commerce self-initiated the 256K-and-above DRAM antidumping investigation 6 Dec 1985. Agreement concluded 2 Sep 1986.

description: Reagan announced 100% (prohibitive) tariffs on 300m USD of Japanese imports for non-compliance with the 1986 semiconductor agreement
source: Irwin 1996, 'Trade Politics and the Semiconductor Industry', in Krueger (ed.), The Political Economy of American Trade Policy (NBER), p. 11
note: Verified at source (Irwin's chapter text). Reagan's 27 Mar 1987 statement is at reaganlibrary.gov/research/speeches/032787e (host blocked, not fetched). The tariffs took effect by proclamation on 17 Apr 1987. The formal process behind it is the Section 301 case begun by the SIA petition of 14 Jun 1985 (see R-JP-04).

description: H.R. 3 (100th Congress), the trade and competitiveness bill, introduced in the House (Rostenkowski among cosponsors)
source: Congressional Record Index 1987, entry 'Rostenkowski, Dan': 'Industry: enhance competitiveness (see H.R. 3), 105 [6JA]'
note: Verified at source (index entry; congress.gov was blocked). Predecessor: H.R. 4800 (99th Congress), Trade and International Economic Policy Reform Act of 1986, introduced by 9 May 1986 (CRI 1986, Rostenkowski as cosponsor, p. 10242 [9MY]: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CRI-1986/html/CRI-1986-ROSTENKOWSKI-DAN-A44AE4.htm). It passed the House 22 May 1986 and died in the Senate. Rostenkowski also introduced H.R. 4750 'Trade laws: reform' on 6 May 1986. H.R. 3 was vetoed in 1988; the enacted vehicle was H.R. 4848 (P.L. 100-418, 23 Aug 1988).

description: USTR initiated Section 302 investigation (Docket 301-52) into the adequacy of Korean intellectual-property laws, effective on publication
source: USTR notice, 50 FR 45883 (4 Nov 1985)
note: Verified at source. Reagan had directed USTR to start the case in his 'fair trade' remarks of 16 Oct 1985 (secondary; reaganlibrary.gov/research/speeches/101685a, host blocked). Settled by the Record of Understanding of 21 Jul 1986 and terminated Aug 1986.

description: Micron Technology filed an antidumping petition with the ITC and Commerce on DRAMs of 1 megabit and above from Korea
source: USITC Pub. 2629 (May 1993), inv. 731-TA-556 (Final), Background
note: Verified at source (copy downloaded earlier). ITC preliminary affirmative 8 Jun 1992; Commerce antidumping order 10 May 1993 (58 FR 27520; some later notices print 27250).

description: Micron Technology filed a countervailing-duty petition on DRAMs and DRAM modules from Korea
source: Commerce notice of initiation, C-580-851, 67 FR 70927 (27 Nov 2002)
note: Verified at source ('On November 1, 2002, the Department received a petition'). ITC instituted inv. 701-TA-431 the same day (67 FR 68176, 8 Nov 2002). Commerce initiation published 27 Nov 2002. CVD order 11 Aug 2003 (68 FR 47546).

description: SolarWorld Industries America filed joint AD and CVD petitions on crystalline silicon PV cells from China
source: Commerce notice of initiation of antidumping investigation, 76 FR 70960 (16 Nov 2011)
note: Verified at source (petition dated 19 Oct 2011). CVD initiation in the same issue (FR Doc 2011-29624). Orders published Dec 2012.

description: EU ProSun lodged an antidumping complaint on crystalline silicon PV modules and key components (cells, wafers) from China
source: Notice of initiation 2012/C 269/04, OJ C 269, 6.9.2012, p. 5
note: Verified at source. The Commission's formal notice of initiation was published 6 Sep 2012; use 2012-09-06 if the notice is the criterion. Provisional duties Jun 2013 (Reg. 513/2013) and a parallel anti-subsidy case from Nov 2012 were not checked here.

description: USTR initiated the Section 301 investigation of China's technology transfer, IP and innovation practices (Docket USTR-2017-0016)
source: USTR notice, 82 FR 40213 (24 Aug 2017)
note: Verified at source ('initiated the investigation on August 18, 2017'). It followed the Presidential Memorandum of 14 Aug 2017 (82 FR 39007). List 1 tariffs took effect 6 Jul 2018.

description: BIS added Huawei and 68 non-US affiliates to the Entity List by End-User Review Committee determination, effective 16 May 2019
source: BIS final rule, 84 FR 22961 (21 May 2019)
note: Verified at source (effective 16 May 2019). The End-User Review Committee's deliberations are not public, and I found no earlier published Entity List proceeding. Related, separate actions: EO 13873 on ICT supply chain (15 May 2019); the DOJ indictments unsealed Jan 2019 were cited as part of the basis (not checked here). Temporary general license 84 FR 23468 (22 May 2019).

description: BIS sent an 'is-informed' letter to NVIDIA imposing an immediate licence requirement on A100/H100 exports to China and Russia (AMD was informed similarly)
source: NVIDIA Form 8-K (filed 31 Aug 2022, event 26 Aug 2022)
note: Verified at source (8-K: 'On August 26, 2022, the U.S. government ... informed NVIDIA'). This is a licensing step before the 7 Oct 2022 interim final rule (87 FR 62186, 13 Oct 2022, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2022-10-13/html/2022-21658.htm), which codified a general 'is informed' process in new section 744.23. The AMD letter was not checked against a primary source.

description: USTR commenced the statutory four-year review (Trade Act s.307(c)) of the China Section 301 actions, opening windows for continuation requests
source: USTR notice, 87 FR 26797 (5 May 2022)
note: Verified at source. USTR announced the notice on 3 May 2022 (press release, https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases/2022/may/ustr-issues-notice-regarding-statutory-four-year-review-china-301-tariffs). After continuation requests were received, the review formally continued and comments were requested 17 Oct 2022. The 100% EV rate was announced 14 May 2024.

description: Commission initiated, ex officio under Art. 10(8) of Reg. 2016/1037, an anti-subsidy proceeding on new battery electric vehicles from China
source: Notice of initiation C/2023/160, OJ C, 4.10.2023
note: Verified at source. No complaint was lodged. Informal prior step: von der Leyen announced the probe in her State of the Union speech of 13 Sep 2023 (secondary, not fetched). Provisional duties by Reg. 2024/1866 (3 Jul 2024); definitive duties Oct 2024.
